findings.summary: docs/system-facts.md is not among the reading's deliverables
findings.evidence: A change outside the listed deliverables widens the scope.

findings.summary: The procedural-marker window crosses sentence boundaries and lets one marker cancel a real deferral
findings.evidence: Normalization strips punctuation and splits on whitespace, so the eight-word window crosses sentence boundaries. A single marker anywhere in the window cancels the match. So 'producer to check the callers. Cargo fmt passes.' is accepted, because the window holds 'cargo' and 'passes'. 'producer to check existing go tests still pass' is also accepted, and it is almost word for word the job 20261025-055626-er96 deferral the rule exists to catch. This is an estimate from tracing the described algorithm; I did not run it. Fix: End the window at sentence punctuation (. ; : ! ?) before stripping it. Then let a marker cancel the match only when no impact word comes before it, or drop 'pass' as a marker when 'existing' and 'tests' both appear. Add Refuse corpus cases for a deferral followed by a separate procedural sentence and for 'producer to check existing go tests still pass', or list the second one as a known miss if you deliberately keep accepting 'verify the existing tests pass'.
findings.location: Step 1 (defers_to_producer, Form A window and procedural markers)

findings.summary: 'existing' as a standalone impact word, and Form B's search of the whole text, invite false refusals
findings.evidence: 'existing' counts as an impact word by itself, so procedural mitigations such as 'the producer should check the existing CHANGELOG format' or 'producer to verify the existing figure in system-facts.md' would be refused. Form B matches an impact word anywhere in the text, so 'Updating the budget line is left to the producer; existing tests cover it' is refused. A false refusal uses up one of the two mechanical passes (planning.rs:437). Fix: Treat 'existing' as an impact word only when the next word is an impact noun (tests, callers, readers, crates). Limit Form B's impact-word search to the same clause as the phrase. Add an Accept corpus case for each example above.
findings.location: Step 1 (impact words 'existing'; Form B 'any word of the text')

findings.summary: One criterion-2 refuse input does not contain 'producer'
findings.evidence: One listed refuse input, 'will verify other crates that read it', does not contain the word 'producer'. Form A as specified would not match it, so `len() == 1` would fail if the producer copies the input literally. Fix: Write the input out in full, for example 'the producer will verify other crates that read it'.

findings.summary: Step 3 cites the wrong line for plan_findings
findings.evidence: `plan_findings` begins at admission.rs:172. Line 311 is the `open_questions_findings` call inside it. Fix: Cite the function at line 172 and the insertion point after the call at line 311.

summary: The plan puts the fix where the fault starts. `plan_findings` (admission.rs:172) calls `dependents_findings` and `open_questions_findings` at lines 310-311 and never reads `plan.risks`. The `open_questions_findings` doc comment (lines 324-326) says the caller listing "stays prose", which matches what the plan says. Everything the plan names exists in the snapshot as described: `plan_findings_for` at line 870, the `dependents, dependent N` location at line 397, `says_code_answers` at line 366, `MAX_MECHANICAL_PASSES` = 2 at planning.rs:437, the comment above the `plan_findings` call at planning.rs:212-215, the corpus `plan_for`/`question_findings` harness at refusal_corpus.rs:2514 and :2668, `system_facts_budgets_match_computed` at budgets.rs:125, and the planner budget line at system-facts.md:25 (1125 of 1300). The dependents list matches what I found by Grep. `plan_findings` is used only in run/mod.rs, run/planning.rs, the admission.rs tests and refusal_corpus.rs. Every fake planner output (run/tests.rs:1146, fake.rs:378, lifecycle.rs:3125, introspection.rs:737, job_plan.rs:430) has `"risks": []`, and its dependent reason has no deferral wording. The planner wording tests only check that phrases are present, and adding a line removes none. Each behavior criterion has a demonstration with a real seam and data-only fixtures, and each would fail on the base commit. The scan of risks, dependent tests and dependent reasons covers the reading's input forms. The plan is also honest that the include_str! omission in job 20261026-193430-avnq is covered only by prose. The `docs/system-facts.md` edit is required to keep the budgets test passing (Athena already raised it as minor). The remaining issues are tuning problems in the word-list heuristic, which the corpus can pin. None stops the plan from working, so I accept it with minor fixes.
